title: The road
body: Three pigs leave home with one cart. The town is a day behind them. Ahead, the road forks around a stand of trees.

title: One house
body: They will share a roof. Straw is in the ditch. Bricks are at the kiln, a week of hauling. They can bring one load before dark.

title: Three loads
body: They divide the cart. You are the youngest, and your sack is the light one. The oldest is already walking toward the kiln.

title: The kiln
body: The oldest will share the bricks if you stay to carry them. A bundle of sticks is closer, and lighter.

title: Straw by dusk
body: The house is up before the light goes. It smells like a dry field. Then the wind changes, and something on the road is coming toward the door.

title: A house of sticks
body: The walls creak when you lean on them. They will do for a night with no weather. There is weather.

title: The brick house
body: The work takes all week. The walls are thick and the door is heavy. The wind comes and pushes. The house does not move. The kettle is already on.

title: Past the trees
body: You run until the straw is behind you. Past the trees a brick house has a light in it. They open the door. The wind keeps going.

title: Through the door
body: The door gives. You get out the back and do not stop. In the morning you start again, and the first load is brick.
